label: early-input g/l/a/n/q/b after d/r/p or l/q/a context
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 99% of mass, peaking at t=2-4 (t=3 alone is 42%). It never fires at t=0 or at the delimiter, and only rarely in the copy phase. The input token is mostly one of g, l, a, n, q, b (g/l/a carry about 60% of mass), usually at its first occurrence. Activation is higher when the prefix contains d (first_tok=d gives 5x lift; the strongest examples start with d d), r or p, or when the previous token is l, q or a (for example d d q [l] q). Rarely fires on most other letters (j, o, x, e) or on digits. The selected predicate (one of six input tokens at t 1-5 AND (d/r/p seen earlier OR prev_tok in l/q/a)) got dev P=0.26, R=0.59, F1=0.36, mass recall 0.70. Tested alternatives: the token+position rule alone got R=0.79 and mass 0.84 but P=0.11. The narrower t 2-4 + d/r/p-seen rule raised P only to 0.29 (F1 0.31). Even the narrowest rules tried stayed below P=0.3, so most matching contexts stay silent. The unit looks like a graded readout of the input token combined with the early prefix contents, not a crisp rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: l, g, a, n; t=1: g, l, a, n; t=3: g, l, a, n) and the previous input (most: l, q, a, h, i, m; least: 2, j, c, t); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, t=2.
